newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Nicaraguan finance chief stresses social policy.
newsitem.headline: Nicaraguan finance chief stresses social policy.

text.p: Nicaragua's finance minister said on Wednesday the new right-wing government would stress social policy and take a tough line against austerity measures imposed by the International Monetary Fund (IMF).
"There are specific instructions from the president to put more emphasis on the social aspects of policy and unemployment," Finance Minister Esteban Duque Estrada said on state-owned television.

The government of President Arnoldo Aleman must deal with the 70 percent of Nicaraguans who live in poverty and the sometimes violent protests of the leftist opposition Sandinista Front, which is opposed to the IMF.

Duque Estrada, who will be in charge of negotiating Nicaragua's structural adjustment programme with the IMF, said the government would take a tougher line in negotiations than that of former President Violeta Chamorro.

Nicaragua's structural adjustment programme, known as ESAF, is suspended due to the Chamorro government's failure to fulfil some of its terms including privatisation of the state telephone company and passage of a tax reform package.

Because of the ESAF suspension, Nicaragua has not received badly needed IMF loans for the past six months. Aleman government officials have said they would probably meet IMF officials within four days to renegotiate the ESAF.

One likely sticking point will be cuts in the public sector payroll. The IMF wants Nicaragua to reduce the size of its payroll but Aleman is under heavy pressure to reduce unemployment and would likely face resistance to any attempts at mass layoffs of state employees, analysts have said.
Some 52 percent of Nicaragua's work force is either unemployed or underemployed, Economy Ministry figures show.
Duque Estrada, a prominent Nicaraguan banker who took over the post on Monday, was a surprise choice as finance minister.
